Predictions of a pruned Random Planted Forest

Source: R/prune.R
predict.rpf_pruned.Rd

The prediction of a pruned forest is alpha + sum(beta_S * f_S(x)) over the kept components f_S of the forest, with the intercept alpha and the coefficients beta_S (see prune_components()).

Usage

# S3 method for class 'rpf_pruned'
predict(object, new_data, nthreads = NULL, ...)

Arguments

object

[rpf_pruned]: A pruned forest from prune_components().

new_data

[data.frame | matrix]: New observations to predict.

nthreads

[integer(1) | NULL: NULL]: Number of threads. NULL uses the nthreads the forest was fitted with.

...

Not currently used, but required for extensibility. Unknown arguments are an error.

Value

A tbl with column .pred with the same number of rows as new_data.

See also

prune_components(), predict_components().

Examples

set.seed(1)
x <- matrix(runif(300 * 3, -1, 1), ncol = 3, dimnames = list(NULL, paste0("x", 1:3)))
y <- x[, 1] + 2 * x[, 2] * x[, 3] + rnorm(300, sd = 0.3)
fit <- rpf(x, y, max_interaction = 2, ntrees = 10, splits = 30)
pruned <- prune_components(fit, x, y, rule = "R", tau = 0.01)
predict(pruned, x[1:5, ])
#> # A tibble: 5 × 1
#>    .pred
#>    <dbl>
#> 1 -0.121
#> 2 -1.46 
#> 3  0.156
#> 4  0.528
#> 5 -1.18
